page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory density. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 extensions, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. High-capacity local storage is bundled directly with the instance, providing 2,880 GB on high-speed NVMe SSD media. The server does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

Performance benchmarks show distinct single-thread strength alongside throughput constraints typical of lower core allocations. In Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, the processor achieved top-quartile results with scores of 2071.0 and 3078.28, respectively. Text processing also demonstrated strong execution speed. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core at 4736.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 6154.66, placed in the median range. Memory bandwidth measurements registered lower efficiency, with uncached read throughput measuring 36.73 GB/sec and small-block cached read reaching 303.46 GB/sec. Application testing reflected average throughput in Redis operations at 6.17 million operations per second, while software compilation and medium-sized language model token processing exhibited lower benchmark percentiles.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the server delivers high resource density by combining dedicated compute cores with substantial fast local NVMe capacity. The principal performance tradeoff involves modest uncached memory throughput and limited parallel core scaling against high local storage volume. Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is appropriately sized for transactional database hosting, NoSQL storage, intermediate ETL staging, search indexing, and in-memory key-value caching where large local disk capacity and consistent single-threaded processing are essential.
description: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of memory, and 2,880 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 vector and cryptographic instruction extensions. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-core execution, placing in the top quartile for Geekbench and stress-ng single-threaded metrics, while multi-core computational throughput scales moderately across its 4 threads. Memory bandwidth and compilation workloads show relative constraints. Providing an expansive local disk footprint and an 8 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance delivers practical efficiency for local scratch caching, relational database hosting, Redis instances, and log processing tasks requiring high local drive capacity and reliable single-thread processing speed.
